newsitem.title: USA: AT&T offers digital PCS service in 40 markets.
newsitem.headline: AT&T offers digital PCS service in 40 markets.

text.p: AT&T Corp. said Wednesday it introduced AT&T Digital PCS, which combines wireless voice, messaging and paging communications via a single telephone, in 40 major markets.

The long distance and wireless phone giant said it will offer AT&T Digital PCS to 70 million potential customers starting Wednesday, and plans to extend it rapidly to more than 212 million more potential customers.

AT&T Digital PCS customers will pay a flat rate in the United States of 60 cents per minute for "roaming" calls -- those calls made from outside the customer's "home," or local, calling area. The company said it will offer a range of service packages, starting at $24.99 per month, with no annual service commitment.
The pager, phone and personal messaging system combination reduces the number of devices, batteries and charging systems customers must have, the company said.

"Our wireless offerings are at the heart of AT&T's delivery of services that meet customers' needs for anytime, anywhere communications," AT&T Chairman Robert Allen said in a statement announcing the service.
AT&T Digital PCS offers customers caller ID, so they can see the number of the person calling, and voice mail, with a message-waiting indicator that alerts them of messages, AT&T said.
With the new service, customers also can receive text and numeric messages on their phones from personal computers and text dispatch services.
Digital technology also offers customers greater privacy and increased resistance to cellular service fraud, AT&T said.

The company said its AT&T Digital PCS is available in major markets, including Seattle; Sacramento, Fresno and Ventura, Calif.; Miami, Tampa, Orlando and West Palm Beach, Fla.; Portland, Ore.; Las Vegas; Salt Lake City; Boise, Idaho; Dallas, San Antonio and Austin, Texas; Oklahoma City and Tulsa, Okla.; Pittsburgh; Minneapolis; and a number of markets in the New York metropolitan area and Northern New Jersey.

AT&T said the devices' battery performance has been dramatically improved, enabling customers to talk longer, or leave their phones on for extended periods of time, using the "sleep mode" feature. Some models can be in a ready mode for as long as 60 hours before recharging is required -- two to three times longer than traditional wireless phones, it said.
Allen scheduled a news conference in Manhattan at 11:30 a.m. (EDT) to announce the launch of the service.
